relationships.subject: PGE2
relationships.evidence_quote: formalin- and prostaglandin E<sub>2</sub>-induced inflammation dramatically increase spinal responses to heating and decrease responses to cooling in male and female mice

relationships.subject: TRPV1-expressing primary sensory neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: The reduction of cold response is largely eliminated on ablation of TRPV1-expressing primary sensory neurons, indicating a crossover inhibition of cold response from the hyperactive heat inputs in the spinal cord.

relationships.subject: oxaliplatin
relationships.evidence_quote: chemotherapy medication oxaliplatin can rapidly increase spinal responses to cooling and suppress responses to heating

key_findings: Inflammation (formalin, PGE2) increases spinal heat and decreases cold responses; the cold reduction depends on TRPV1 neurons (crossover inhibition).
Oxaliplatin rapidly increases spinal cold and suppresses heat responses, indicating a push-pull mechanism.
